title: Natural Hypertrophy Training Playlist
summary: NH releases his personal ~360-song training playlist on Spotify as a Christmas present and explains how he built it over 15 years. He gives advice on composing a training playlist: mix genres, balance PR songs with transitional and joke songs, keep it for working sets, and build your own like a program.
claims: His training playlist is the result of about 15 years of curation, started at age 11; a song only stays if he still loves it after repeated listening over time
The playlist has around 360 songs, enough to take weeks or a month of training to get through
Put the playlist on shuffle, don't skim or skip songs, and let songs surprise you while you build memories with them as you lift
A playlist of only hard metal or only hype songs makes the body habituate, so it no longer triggers an adrenaline boost
Listen to podcasts or something educational during warm-ups and keep the music for working sets so it stays special
Structure a playlist with PR songs that get you pumped immediately, transitional songs for warm-ups or high-rep sets, and joke songs
Joke songs remind you that you're just a guy doing squats, creating a dip in intensity that releases stress before getting back to it
A playlist is like a program, a reflection of your soul; build your own rather than following someone else's
Be open to every genre and portion the playlist out, e.g. 40 PR songs, 30 transition, 10 classical
Include patriotic music from your own country because pride is motivating
Around 300 songs is a good playlist size; 2000 is too many because you never hear each song often enough
